title: Answer to Question: Bhutto, Musharraf and the Developments of the Situation in Pakistan
text:
Answer to Question

Bhutto, Musharraf and the Developments of the Situation in Pakistan

Question: What made America, which is dominant over the rule in Pakistan, agree to pardon Bhutto and return her to Pakistan, when she was imbued with loyalty to the English during the eight years she spent in London, she and her followers?

Then, where is Pakistan heading amid those successive events?

Answer: The answer to this question requires going back a little:

1 - Matters began to accelerate in Pakistan after the arrival of Bush and the neoconservatives at the seat of power in America, and especially after the bombings of the eleventh of September, when the American invasion of Afghanistan was a decisive factor in the Pakistani President, America's greatest agent in the region, Pervez Musharraf, standing with the Americans in their invasion of Afghanistan, and in their war against the Mujahideen Muslims inside Pakistan itself. Musharraf's joining America in its declared war on terrorism (Islam) was tantamount to a declaration of the mounting of a new crusader military campaign against the Kashmiri and Pakistani jihadi currents and movements which had taken Pakistan as a stronghold and launching ground for themselves.

By this alliance of his with the Americans, Musharraf succeeded in depriving these Mujahideen of their stronghold and safe base in Pakistan, so he succeeded in what all the previous Pakistani governments had failed in, in their attempts to close the camps of the Mujahideen, pursue them, arrest them and consider them terrorists.

This traitor presented the greatest gift to India, which for decades had been unable to dissuade Pakistan from supporting these Mujahideen. The hearts of the Hindus were gladdened by that, and they merged completely with the new vocabulary which the Bush administration launched in fighting (Islamic terrorism), as they describe it, and considered the jihadi Kashmiri resistance one of the colours of terrorism. In this consideration the current Congress government, with its English tendencies, did not differ from the previous Janata government with its American inclinations.

2 - Moreover, the American officials have not stopped demanding more from Musharraf, because whoever is made lowly, lowliness becomes easy upon him. An official in American intelligence threatened in the New York Times on 23/7/2007 CE to pound the tribal region, and the American Director of Intelligence Mike McConnell said two days after that that Osama bin Laden is present in an area in Pakistan on the border with Afghanistan, and urged (Musharraf) to do more in massing armies in the border region.

Yes, the American administration has not been content with the services the Pakistani army has provided to the Americans on the border; rather, it demands more of it, so that it carries out on its behalf the difficult and dirty tasks.

The American administration wants Musharraf to continue following the same approach he followed in his fighting of the Islamic currents such as al-Qaeda, the Taliban, Harakat al-Mujahideen (formerly al-Ansar), the organisation Jaish-e-Mohammed and other movements, and to secure the Afghan-Pakistani border, which reaches 1500 kilometres, and to prevent the fighters from using Pakistani territory to launch against the American and Atlantic occupation in Afghanistan, and to declare all-out and decisive war against the tribesmen supporting the Taliban and al-Qaeda.

Perhaps the visit of Negroponte, the Deputy Secretary of State, who specialises in igniting civil wars and shedding blood, to Islamabad in July 2007 was aimed at achieving these goals through the continued presence in power of Musharraf, who has grown accustomed to betraying the Muslims and has devoted himself to serving the Americans. Negroponte admitted that in his visit to Pakistan he discussed the matter of directing a military strike inside the tribal areas.

3 - Musharraf has become accustomed to the policy of the big stick which America uses against him, for he is an obedient agent who carries out orders even if they are flagrantly against the interest of his people and his country. For this reason the Americans described him as a (treasure), for he is a guaranteed agent who fulfils all the American conditions in an inflamed region such as Pakistan.

He has defied the feelings of the Muslims, stood with America in its aggression on Afghanistan, and made Pakistan an advanced American line in the aggression on Afghanistan.

He is massing armies in the tribal region on the Afghan border in Waziristan and Baluchistan, and the number of Pakistani military forces stationed on the Pakistani-Afghan border has been raised from 80 thousand to 90 thousand. And today, 26/10/2007, he is launching a violent attack on the Muslims in the Swat valley north-east of Peshawar because they want to implement the raising of the standing of Islam.

All of that is to ignite the bloody war which Washington wants and continually pushes its agent Musharraf to carry out between Muslims: the Pakistani army on one side and the Muslim tribes on the other, in a provocative manner so that the fire remains burning. Musharraf dealt with the protest movements against Musharraf's link to America the way one who wants to ignite a civil war deals, not the way one who wants to reach a solution to the protest movements deals, as he did when he deliberately killed the leader of the movement in Baluchistan, Akbar Khan Bugti, aged 79, in August 2006 CE; so the movements increased and became more inflamed, which made the crisis worse. Bugti was known by the title «the old lion», and he held the post of governor and chief minister in the late seventies in the province of Baluchistan.

4 - When the Pakistani army was compelled, in the wake of the killing of Bugti and the effective escalation of the movements against Musharraf's army, when the army was compelled to conclude an agreement with the tribes to calm matters in September 2006, America was not pleased with that. So America, under the name of NATO, carried out a bloody attack in the border area of Bajaur in November 2006 to spoil the agreement with the tribes. Then the American officials intensified their statements criticising the agreement and urged (Musharraf) to mass armies in the tribal region, all of that so that the agreement would not hold. And this is what happened: Rice criticised the agreement in her speech before Congress on 16/2/2007, and Cheney, the American Vice-President, criticised it on the same day during his visit to Pakistan. Likewise Musharraf carried out Washington's wish by massing armies on the border in a manner provocative to the tribes, in escalating steps to cancel the agreement. This shows clearly that America does not want to calm the region peacefully, but rather wants the war between Muslims to remain burning, so that they turn away from resisting its occupation of Afghanistan; and it has found in Musharraf a treasure, as they described him, for carrying out their aims.

After that, and to spur Pakistan to do more in attacking the tribes and al-Qaeda, the official spokesman of the White House, Tony Snow, stated that al-Qaeda poses a great threat to Pakistan, therefore they are studying the possibility of carrying out a special operation against specific al-Qaeda targets inside Pakistan.

This is what pushed the Pakistani Prime Minister Shaukat Aziz to state that they are able to carry out such an operation themselves and that they will never allow Pakistani territory to be used as a launching ground for the activities of any terrorist organisation. Thus he tried to justify the operations which Pakistan launches against the Muslims on the pretext that unless we carry out the operations, America will intervene and carry them out itself!

5 - Following that, the heinous attack on the Lal Masjid (the Red Mosque) took place in mid-July 2007, and in its wake the previous agreement concluded between the army and the tribes ended, and a state of actual war came about; but not between aggressor America and the Muslims, as it ought to be, but between the Muslim tribes and the Pakistani army, which reinforced its forces in the face of the tribes on the orders of Musharraf and his treacherous administration. America announced, through Bush's National Security Adviser Stephen Hadley, that it views these military reinforcements positively and that it supports them.

Thus Musharraf's hostility towards the tribal region appeared. And what escalated matters further was what was exposed during Musharraf's aggression on the Red Mosque of cruelty, criminality and massacres, and total refusal of any negotiations, and breaking them off suddenly after there had been successful mediations, and what followed that of the humiliation of the sheikhs and mullahs during and after their arrest or killing!

This is about Musharraf's hostility towards the tribes.

6 - As for Kashmir, the solution offered by America is that the situation remains as it is regarding the borders, to please India, which America wishes to become a rival to China in the Far East and South-East Asia. Musharraf has proceeded in several steps to normalise the fait accompli, after the two countries reached a ceasefire in Kashmir in November 2003 and resumed (peace) negotiations between them in January 2004, which allowed the reopening of symbolic crossings for buses in Kashmir between India and Pakistan, and the two sides proceeded in steps strengthening economic trade relations to normalise the current situation. This solution is the one currently offered by India: the Indian Prime Minister Manmohan Singh said on 15/07/2007 CE that the divided region of Kashmir can become a symbol of cooperation between India and Pakistan, and that the talks aimed at ending 60 years of conflict will continue. Manmohan Singh affirmed his position that: «borders cannot be changed, but they can be made irrelevant», meaning not hostile borders. And he said, in a speech while receiving an honorary degree in Jammu, the winter capital of the state of Jammu and Kashmir, a copy of which was sent to Reuters by e-mail: «There can be no doubt about the divisions and barriers remaining, but the Line of Control, the border, can become a line of peace with a greater flow of freedom of ideas, goods and services for the people». Singh added: «I hope and trust that Jammu and Kashmir can one day become a symbol of cooperation between India and Pakistan instead of conflict.»

The current reality testifies that this solution is the one Musharraf is proceeding in with India, and all the statements relating to Kashmir from the Pakistani side in the recent period no longer go outside this framework. Since the negotiations of 2004 CE, the right of self-determination for the people of Kashmir is no longer a subject of discussion for Musharraf's Pakistan, and it has not demanded it as it used to do, and Musharraf's government no longer demands, as in the past, negotiations on the basis of the international resolutions, let alone restoring Kashmir through Jihad. This means that matters are proceeding towards ceding Kashmir and entrenching the existing situation as a final solution for Kashmir.

7 - Thus Musharraf has cut his ties with Islam and the Muslims:

He stood with America in its aggression on Afghanistan, mobilised armies in a bloody attack in the tribal region, committing massacres in Waziristan and Baluchistan, bombarded the Red Mosque with weapons of destruction, lost Kashmir, humiliated the scholars and the students of the Islamic schools, and arrested the carriers of the Islamic Da'wah...

Accordingly, he has become an outcast, rejected by the Muslims, and found himself exposed without (popularity) before his desire for the presidency for a second term. At that point America had no way of preserving its (treasure) except to turn to the secularists of the English, that is, to Benazir Bhutto and her party, by concluding a deal with her through which Bhutto would become pure and clean of her corruption and corrupting, of which Musharraf had previously accused her and then exiled her from the country. Under the deal, he issued a decree pardoning her on 5/10/2007, that is, before the presidential elections which he brought forward to 6/10/2007, when they ought to have taken place after the parliamentary elections in January 2008. But he feared that his partisans would fall in the coming parliamentary elections in January 2008, which would make the new parliamentary body electing him to a second presidency hard to attain; so he brought the presidential elections ahead of the parliamentary elections, since the old parliament had been elected before his scandals spread, which made some people deceived by him and vote in his favour in the previous elections. Thus he won the elections which took place on 6/10/2007 according to the previous parliamentary electoral body!

8 - A division emerged in the Pakistani government over the project of pardoning Bhutto, as a number of members of the ruling «League» party considered dropping the charges «unfair». The Minister of Religious Affairs Ijaz-ul-Haq, "the son of the former military dictator Zia-ul-Haq, who executed Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, Benazir's father, in 1979", said: «We have expressed our reservations about the offer of the proposed pardon, and we do not support it». And he stressed the obligation of «not granting a pardon to corrupt politicians, especially those accused of plundering 1.5 billion dollars», in reference to the opposition leader.

It is not strange that the opposition should appear from within Musharraf's party, for the manner of the founding of this party makes that clear. Musharraf brought his party (the Pakistan Muslim League party) into being from politicians whom he made split from the Pakistan Muslim League party (Nawaz Sharif), and likewise from politicians who split from the Pakistan People's Party (Benazir Bhutto), by threatening them with corruption if they did not submit to him. And it is not strange that in a party such as this contradictory opinions should appear in times of crisis.

9 - But because the matter is bigger than Musharraf's party, the opposition had no effect at all. Rather, despite the opposition of some elements of his party, the Pakistani President Pervez Musharraf and the former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto reached on 04/10/2007 CE the agreement of the deal which America and Britain managed, as a prelude to the sharing of power between them. It was followed by the aforementioned pardon decree on 5/10/2007, that is, 24 hours before the presidential elections, which the court approved being held on their date. The consequence of this pardon was that Bhutto's party did not boycott the election of the President as the opposition parties did, and by that the quorum was secured, and then victory for Musharraf with a second presidency!

That pardon was part of the (National Reconciliation) decree, which stipulates dropping the prosecution of politicians before the courts for crimes relating to corruption. Before the presidential signing of that decree, the government ratified it.

The decree allows the pardon of politicians whose charges attributed to them go back to the period extending from 1988 until 1999. It was drafted in this manner so as not to include the former Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, whom Musharraf overthrew in a white coup in 1999, because the criminal cases brought against him go back to 2000.

Thus the pardon was drafted so as not to include Nawaz Sharif, despite his being a former agent of America; but it became angry with him when he was unable to prevent the movement of the feelings of the Pakistani army in coming to the aid of the Kashmiri Mujahideen against the Indian army on the heights of Kargil, which inflicted a defeat on the Indian army at the time in 1999, and whose continuation almost undermined the rule of Vajpayee, who was loyal to America. Therefore America toppled him at the hand of Musharraf in 1999, and Musharraf carried out America's order and returned the Pakistani army to its positions before the occupation of the Kargil heights. America did not overlook that (slip) of Nawaz Sharif despite his serving it for years. If the agents had any sense, they would take a lesson from others and know that the colonialist state casts out its agent, however much he has served it, when it has exhausted its purposes from him.

After the mentioned pardon decision issued on 5/10/2007, and after securing the election of Musharraf on 6/10/2007, then after the Supreme Court began examining the validity of the presidential elections from 17/10/2007 and did not annul the validity of the elections (up to today, despite its repeated meetings to study the results of the elections), Bhutto returned on 18/10/2007, she who held the premiership twice, from 1988 to 1990 and from 1993 to 1996, and who aspires to the premiership for the third time after the parliamentary elections in January 2008.

10 - America exerted effort in concluding the deal with Bhutto, all of it to guarantee that its (treasure) Musharraf remains in power. Had Bhutto boycotted, as the opposition did, it would not have been possible for Musharraf to win a second presidency.

America began the talks on the deal with the English and Bhutto in London for several months, until the broad lines of the future sharing of power were arranged, between Musharraf as head of state and Bhutto as Prime Minister. America did that while knowing that Bhutto does not accept being a Prime Minister with the current powers, but rather having actual authority which she shares with the authority of the President of the Republic. But, as it is said, (your brother is compelled, not a hero); for Musharraf remaining with the loss of some powers to Bhutto is better than America's influence in Pakistan disappearing.

After that, and in light of the basic steps which America took, the talks began between Musharraf and Bhutto, sometimes directly and at other times between their envoys, sometimes in London and at other times in the Emirates... and so on, to bring about balanced steps between the two parties, with a concession here and gains there. Musharraf agreed to remove any legal obstacles to Bhutto's return (clean) of all corruption charges, and likewise to enact legislation, if necessary, to facilitate Bhutto's assuming the premiership for the third time, since she had previously held it twice, and not to harass her party in contesting the new elections at the beginning of next year...; and she agreed that her party would not boycott the parliament as the opposition did, and that her followers in the Supreme Court would not stand against Musharraf's candidacy for the presidency before he takes off his military uniform, except after his success...

And matters proceeded according to what they had agreed:

The deputies of the People's Party, which Bhutto leads, refrained from boycotting the parliament as the other opposition deputies did.

The Supreme Court (the Election Commission) reorganised the laws of the election of the head of state issued in 1998, and the chief of the court, who is opposed to Musharraf and loyal to Bhutto, was absent, to make it easy for the remaining members to cancel article (63), which had formed an obstacle for Musharraf; consequently he was permitted to stand as a candidate before taking off his military uniform. At the same time the secretary of Musharraf's party, the Pakistan Muslim «League» party, stated that after Musharraf is elected for the second time he will take off his uniform.

On 27 September, when nominations for the elections for the presidency of the state began, Musharraf stated that he would abide by the decision of the Supreme Court on the permissibility of his candidacy, when this permissibility was already guaranteed! The Supreme Court (the Election Commission) had issued, on the last day of nominations, a decision in Musharraf's favour. On 29 September the Election Commission examined 43 applications, and from among them 6 applications were chosen, one of them Musharraf's application. Among those whose applications were accepted was Amin Fahim, one of the supporters of Benazir Bhutto, but he said that if Musharraf stands he would withdraw his candidacy. So by that there remained Musharraf and his rival Wajihuddin Ahmed, in addition to three other candidates.

On 01 October, when the final official lists of candidates were announced, 85 parliamentary deputies resigned, including the supporters of Nawaz Sharif, but Bhutto's deputies continued! On 02 October one of Musharraf's ministers announced that Benazir Bhutto would not be criminalised, and directly after that Musharraf announced that if he is elected head of state anew he would give up the post of chief of staff. He nominated one of those close to him to succeed him as chief of staff, the former head of intelligence Ashfaq Kayani, since Musharraf sees that Kayani can be accepted by Bhutto, or at least without objection to him, when she takes over the headship of the government, because Kayani was the one who led the government delegation in Musharraf's name during the months of talks with Bhutto's aides.

Then the pardon decision was issued on 5/10/2007, Musharraf won the elections on 6/10/2007, the Supreme Court did not annul the results of the presidential elections, and Bhutto arrived on 18/10/2007. Matters proceeded smoothly, their clarity disturbed only by the assassination attempt to which Bhutto was exposed during the procession of her motorcade. It is unlikely that Musharraf is behind the attempt, given his need for her, (at least) to get past the stage of the new elections at the beginning of next year. Nevertheless, as we mentioned, some wings of the rule, especially those associated with Zia-ul-Haq, protested against the pardon of Bhutto; and were it not that the Bhutto deal is a vital matter for America and Musharraf at the present time, that deal would not have been concluded.

From the above, the reasons and motives become clear which made America accept concluding the deal with Bhutto, while it knows fully that she was imbued with loyalty to the English during the eight years she spent in exile.

As for where Pakistan is heading amid those events: Pakistan, since its creation about sixty years ago, has not been ruled by two colours but by one colour: the men of the English, then the men of America. For the first time in its history it will be ruled by two heads: Musharraf, whose loyalty is to America, and Bhutto, whose loyalty is to the English; this is if commitment to implementing the deal that was concluded continues. This makes the situation in Pakistan exposed to struggle and turmoil after a period that is not far off.

As was explained previously, America was compelled into the Bhutto deal to save Musharraf from falling, and consequently to preserve its influence in Pakistan, even if it is somewhat diminished due to the transfer of some powers to Bhutto and the English.

What is expected is the continuation of the (good) implementation of the concluded deal, (at least) until the coming elections, for Musharraf and Bhutto both need that:

Musharraf, to bring about an alliance in the parliament of his party and Bhutto's party so as to enable Musharraf to issue the necessary decisions; and Bhutto, to bring about a weight in the parliament for her party that enables her to reach the headship of the government with a legal formation (the majority party).

Even though they are both (secularists) and fight Islam and the Muslims, and their statements expose that, and what their breasts conceal is greater, the fact that they are agents of two different parties will not make their meeting last long.

That is because the struggle of the major states over influence does not accept stopping halfway, especially when one of its two parties is America, with its arrogance and conceit. Therefore America and Musharraf will fabricate problems for Bhutto, legally and materially, to reduce her size, and indeed to exile her again if they can. At the same time the English and Bhutto, with the customary English malice and likewise with political cunning, will set about stirring up the bad things in Musharraf's conduct (and there is a great, great deal of it), so that an issue, nay issues, are made out of them to shake Musharraf's remaining in the presidency of the republic, and indeed to remove him if they can, whether that be through political actions or through judicial actions, by moving their men in the Supreme Court against Musharraf anew...

Thus what is expected is struggle between the two parties, politically and materially, and this has two faces:

Negative, in that the unrest and instability resulting from the struggle make people's lives difficult and anxious,

And positive, in that the strength of the two parties will be exhausted, by the permission of Allah, and Allah takes revenge on one oppressor by means of another oppressor, then takes revenge on both of them; and Allah is Mighty, Wise.

And in this there is good, if Allah wills, for the Nusrah and its people. "And Allah has full power over His affair, but most of the people do not know."

15 Shawwal 1428 AH

26/10/2007 CE
